title: Food as theology
hookLine: the langar teaches equality through a meal

lines: A STRIP OF CLOTH, A SINGLE ROW.
cards: A long strip of cloth runs down the hall floor, and people sit along it, cross-legged, in a single row. A volunteer comes down the line with a steel bucket and a ladle, and a scoop of dal lands on each tray.
Then a roti, dropped into hands held open. The person on your left might be a taxi driver. On your right, a doctor, or a student, or someone who hasn't eaten since yesterday.
Nobody asks. Nobody pays. The food is simple, and it's the same for everyone in the row.
This is langar, and to Sikhs it's more than a free lunch. A meal can teach.

teach.b: First, langar itself: the Guru's kitchen, cooked and served by volunteers and open to anyone who comes. Sikhs trace it back to Guru Nanak, and it's kept in gurdwaras to this day. Second, the Granth remembers it.

teach.h: MATA KHIVI, PRAISED IN THE GRANTH.
teach.b: In a ballad by the musicians Balwand and Satta, the langar of Guru Angad's time is praised, and so is Mata Khivi, Guru Angad's wife.
In paraphrase, she is a good woman who gives cool shade like a leafy tree, and in the langar the Guru's wealth is shared out: rich kheer, made with ghee.
Notice what scripture praises here: a kitchen, and the woman running it. Third, the row.

teach.h: PANGAT: ONE ROW, EVEN AN EMPEROR.
teach.b: The meal is eaten in pangat, sitting in a line on the same floor. In a society where rules about who could eat with whom marked people as higher and lower, sitting in one row said something without a single word.
Tradition says that when the emperor Akbar came to meet Guru Amar Das, he was asked to eat in the langar first, and he sat in the row with everyone else.

teach.h: A BELIEF BECOMES A SEATING PLAN.
teach.b: First the row, then the meeting. Fourth, why call this theology. Sikh teaching says the one Light is in every person.

You can say that in a sermon. Or you can hand everyone the same bowl, at the same height, from the same pot, and let them notice who is sitting next to them. A belief about God becomes a seating plan.

how: Gurdwaras serve langar, a free vegetarian meal cooked and served by volunteers, to anyone who comes; people traditionally sit together in rows on the floor, in pangat.

games.q: you're the emperor Akbar, come to meet Guru Amar Das. you're told that visitors eat in the langar first. what do you do?

games.why: tradition says Akbar sat in the pangat and ate with everyone before meeting the Guru. first the row, then the meeting.

practice: Bring to mind the people you usually eat with, then let your mind wander wider: a coworker you've never had lunch with, a neighbor, an older relative, someone whose life looks nothing like yours.
Let one face come forward, and picture the two of you at the same table, same food, same height. Breathe out, and let the picture stay a while.

wordCard.voice: Food as theology. The langar teaches that the Light is in everyone by seating everyone in one row, with the same food. Today's word.
